sentences.text: 2 2. Petitioners and sixth respondent are into purified drinking water business.

Fifth respondent in terms of policy for providing pure drinking water to the people of the jurisdiction of fifth respondent proceeded to award contract to the sixth respondent for installation of water purifying units at the respective places stated by the fifth respondent.

Accordingly, fifth respondent has entered into agreement for a period of five years for 12 units in different wards as is evident from Annexures 'E'
and 'F'.
No doubt such agreement executed by fifth respondent with the sixth respondent is not for any monitory gain by the fifth respondent.
Therefore, question of inviting tender and other process to commence water purifying units at identified places in the respective wards of fifth respondent is territorial jurisdiction.
Sixth respondent after installation of water purifier units at the respective places he is charging certain amount to the general public to supply purified drinking water.
Such an act is nothing but providing service through fifth respondent.

3. Time and again Courts have held that in respect of any public service like providing infrastructure and award of contract with or without any profit to the respective public institutions formalities are required to be followed like inviting tender from the respective and eligible parties.
In other words Article 14 of the Constitution is to be adhered.

4. In the present case fifth respondent without resorting to tender or giving opportunity to eligible persons to participate in installing water purification units at the respective places stated in Annexure-E and proceeded to enter into an agreement with the sixth respondent is highly arbitrary and is illegal, since fifth respondent has not resorted to tender or notifying in the news paper for installation of water purification units at the respective places.
If the sixth respondent is charging more money for supplying drinking water to the public that is required to be regulated.

Therefore,
fifth respondent in the interest of public he has to notified in the news paper even though if there is no profit to the fifth respondent arising out of installation of water purifier units at the respective places at the same time sixth respondent is charging reasonable amount to the general public in supplying drinking water is to be ascertained only in a competitive bid in a tender, in not adopting the aforesaid procedure like notifying in the news paper or wide publication so as to provide opportunity to the persons who are similarly situated like petitioner and sixth respondent.

5. Supreme Court in the case of Tata Cellular vs. Union of India, reported in (1994) 6 Supreme Court Cases 651 held as under :

sentences.text: It cannot be denied that the principles of judicial review would apply to the exercise of contractual powers by Government bodies in order to prevent arbitrariness or favoritism.
However, it must be clearly stated that there are inherent limitations in exercise of that power of judicial review.
Government is the guardian of the finances of the State.
It is expected to protect the financial interest of the State.
The right to refuse the lowest or any other tender is always available to the Government.
But, the principles laid down in Article 14 of the Constitution have to be kept in view while accepting or refusing a tender.
There can be no question of infringement of Article 14 if the Government tries to get the best person or the best quotation.
The right to choose cannot be considered to be an arbitrary power.

Judicial quest in administrative matters has been to find the right balance between the administrative discretion to decide matters whether contractual or political in nature or issues of social policy; thus they are not essentially justifiable and the need to remedy any unfairness.
Such an unfairness is set right by judicial review.
"73. Observance of judicial restraint is currently the mood in England.
The judicial power of review is exercised to rein in any unbridled executive functioning.
The restraint has two contemporary manifestations.
One is the ambit of judicial intervention; the other covers the scope of the court's ability to quash an administrative decision on its merits.

These restraints bear the hallmarks of judicial control over administrative action."
6.
Accordingly, Annexures 'E' and 'F' are set- aside.
Reserving liberty to fifth respondent to proceed in accordance with law for installation of pure drinking water units at the respective places after following due process of law.
The above exercise shall be completed within a period of three months from today.
In the meanwhile sixth respondent is permitted to supply pure drinking water to the general public till 31.07.2019 in order to avoid hardship to the general public during summer season.
Accordingly, writ petitions stand disposed of.
